subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
source: Adapted from the school Drive Quran folder (TPS Quran Tracker: tajweed rules by year, Years 1-6 progression); Qur'an text per the Madinah mushaf (Hafs 'an 'Asim)

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Beginning a recitation
lessons.title: Isti'adha and Basmalah: four ways to join
objectives: Recite the isti'adha and basmalah correctly
Know why we say them
Know the four ways to join them to the start of a surah

keywords.def: seeking refuge in Allah from Shaytan: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ

starter: Bismillah. Name the three kinds of madd that need 4 counts or more.
Is the laam in بِسْمِ اللَّهِ heavy or light?

teach.heading: Why we seek refuge
bullets: Allah tells us in the Qur'an to seek refuge before reciting
teach.note: Read the ayah meaning: when you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge with Allah from the accursed Shaytan (16:98). Explain that it protects our hearts and attention. Say it together slowly. Ask: what do we ask Allah for?

teach.heading: The basmalah
bullets: We begin every surah with it, except At-Tawbah
It is part of Al-Fatihah in the mushaf
teach.note: Surah 9 (At-Tawbah) begins without a basmalah. The basmalah is written at the top of other surahs in the mushaf. Check the laam of Allah (light, after kasrah) and the madd in الرَّحْمَٰنِ.

teach.heading: Four correct ways
bullets: 3. Join isti'adha + basmalah, stop, start the surah
4. Stop after isti'adha, join basmalah + surah
teach.note: Use a simple example with Surat Al-Ikhlas. Demonstrate each way slowly. Tell pupils that all four are accepted; the thing to avoid is joining the end of the previous surah to the basmalah when starting a new surah. Practise each way twice.

teach.heading: Practise
bullets: Choose one way and be consistent
teach.note: Pupils pick a way and use it throughout the term. Pair work: one recites, one names which way was used. Praise careful breath control.

practice: What are the four ways of joining? Name two.
independent: Recite the isti'adha + basmalah + Al-Ikhlas in way 1, then way 2
Pairs: guess which of the four ways your partner used
Write the isti'adha and basmalah from memory
exit: Which ayah tells us to seek refuge?
lessons.homework: Recite the isti'adha and basmalah before each recitation at home this week.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: audio of each way and a flow chart. Stretch: explain the difference between ways 3 and 4.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Makharij - where letters come from
lessons.title: Makharij: the five areas and the throat
objectives: Know what makharij means
Name the five general areas
Find the three throat positions

keywords.def: the place a letter comes from (plural: makharij)
the empty space of the mouth and throat

starter: Name the 15 ikhfa letters (as far as you can).

teach.heading: Where letters live
teach.note: Ask: how do we know where a sound comes from? Pupils say 'ba' and 'ka' and feel the difference. Introduce makharij as the practical heart of tajweed.

teach.heading: The five areas
bullets: Ash-Shafatan: the lips, Al-Khayshum: the nose
teach.note: Write the five on the board with a quick body map. The scholars divide these into 17 specific points; Year 4 learns the five areas, then Year 5 onwards revisits more detail. Ask pupils to touch each area.

teach.heading: Throat letters
teach.note: Say each pair slowly with a hand on the throat. Compare ح (middle of the throat) with ه (deepest part of the throat). Compare غ and خ (khaa is breathy, ghayn is voiced). Pupils repeat each pair.

teach.heading: Practice
bullets: Say each pair with a vowel
teach.note: Do a call-and-response drill: teacher says a letter, pupils say heavy/light plus the area. Use a mirror if on camera.

practice: Which throat letters are in the middle?
independent: Match 10 letters to the five areas
Read words with throat letters from Al-Fatihah (e.g. الْحَمْدُ, نَعْبُدُ, الْمَغْضُوبِ)
Pairs: say a throat letter and the partner names its area
lessons.homework: Say the six throat letters daily with a hand on your throat and say which position each comes from.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: body-map diagram with labels. Stretch: describe the difference between ح and ه.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Makharij - where letters come from
lessons.title: Makharij: the tongue
objectives: Name tongue letter groups
Say qaaf and kaaf from different places
Say the letters from the tip of the tongue

keywords.def: where ل ن ر and others begin

starter: Which of ح ه is breathier?
Say the five areas in order.

teach.heading: The tongue has the most letters
bullets: 18 of the 28 letters come from the tongue
We divide the tongue into parts
teach.note: Explain that the tongue has several points, taught in groups. Pupils need not memorise numbers; they need to feel the places. Ask: which letters have you already felt in the tongue?

teach.heading: Back of the tongue
bullets: Both touch the roof of the mouth
teach.note: Say قُلْ and كُلْ with a pair. Qaaf is deeper and heavy; kaaf is lighter and further forward. Pupils feel the difference. Connect to the meaning mix-up from Year 3.

teach.heading: Middle of the tongue
bullets: The middle of the tongue meets the roof
teach.note: Say the three letters and feel the middle of the tongue rise. Sheen has air; jeem is a stop; yaa is smooth. Use words from known surahs.

teach.heading: Tip of the tongue
bullets: ل  ن  ر - tip meets the gum above the teeth
ط  د  ت - tip touches base of top front teeth
ظ  ذ  ث - tip between the teeth
teach.note: Say each trio with a vowel. Ask pupils to look at their camera or a mirror: for ظ ذ ث the tip is visible. Highlight the difference between ث and س, ظ and ز. For ص ز س the tip is near the lower front teeth and the sound whistles.

practice: Say قُلْ and كُلْ. What is different?
Which letters have the tip between the teeth?
independent: Match 12 tongue letters to back, middle or tip
Read word pairs: ثَ/سَ, ذَ/زَ, طَ/تَ
Practise Al-Falaq ayah 1 and say where each letter is from
exit: Name two letters from the back of the tongue.
Which letters come from the middle?
lessons.homework: Say the pairs ثَ/سَ, ذَ/زَ, طَ/تَ and قَ/كَ every day, looking in a mirror.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: mouth-diagram cards with arrows. Stretch: explain how the tongue changes for ظ and ز.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: Makharij - where letters come from
lessons.title: Makharij: lips, jawf and khayshum
objectives: Name the lip letters
Understand the jawf and madd
Understand ghunnah from the nose

keywords.def: the nasal passage, source of ghunnah

teach.heading: The lips
bullets: ب  م  و - the two lips
ف - the teeth touch the inside of the lower lip
teach.note: Say ب and م: the lips close. Say و: lips make a small round. Say ف: upper teeth touch the lower lip. Pupils feel each. Examples: بِسْمِ, فِي, وَ.

teach.heading: The jawf: the empty space
bullets: The three madd letters come from the jawf
The sound travels, no tongue touches
teach.note: Say the three madd letters long. Notice nothing touches the mouth; the sound fills the open space. Link to natural madd of two counts.

teach.heading: The khayshum: the nose
teach.note: Pupils hum and feel the vibration at the nose. Recap the rules that use ghunnah. Ask: which letters always have ghunnah when doubled? Noon and meem.

teach.heading: Quiz
bullets: Say a letter, name the area
Throat, tongue, lips, jawf or nose
teach.note: Run a quick-fire quiz with a list of 15 letters. Include madd letters and noon. Keep it light and positive.

practice: Name the two lip letters that close the lips.
independent: Complete a map of all five areas with example letters
Read Al-Falaq and write the area of each underlined letter
Pairs: quiz each other on 10 letters
lessons.homework: Teach a family member the five areas of makharij and give an example letter for each.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: colour-coded letter chart by area. Stretch: explain the difference between ب and م.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Laam and stopping signs
lessons.title: Laam of Al: sun and moon letters
objectives: Know the definite article الْ
Name the sun and moon letters
Read laam shamsiyyah and qamariyyah correctly

keywords.def: the laam of Al is not pronounced before sun letters
the laam is pronounced clearly before moon letters

teach.heading: The word Al
bullets: It is added to the start of a word
The laam may be said or not said
teach.note: Show الشَّمْسُ and الْقَمَرُ. Ask: what do you notice? In one the laam is silent and the next letter is doubled. In the other the laam is pronounced.

teach.heading: Moon letters: say the laam
bullets: ا ب ج ح خ ع غ ف ق ك م ه و ي
teach.note: Count the 14 letters. Examples: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ (Al-Fatihah), الْفَلَقِ (Al-Falaq). The laam has a sukoon and is clear. Pupils echo.

teach.heading: Sun letters: join in
bullets: ت ث د ذ ر ز س ش ص ض ط ظ ل ن
teach.note: Examples: النَّاسِ (An-Nas) and الصَّمَدُ (Al-Ikhlas). The laam is silent and the next letter takes a shaddah. Pupils find the shaddah.

teach.heading: Other laam sakinah
teach.note: Briefly note that the laam in قُلْ (a command) and هَلْ (a particle) is always said clearly. The point for this term: only the laam of الْ follows the sun/moon rule.

practice: Is the laam in الشَّمْسُ said or silent?
independent: Sort 14 words into sun or moon
Underline the Al words in Al-Falaq and An-Nas and label them
Pairs: read and label each other's list
exit: What is a sun letter? Give an example.
What happens to the laam before a moon letter?
lessons.homework: Find five Al words in Al-Fatihah and label them sun or moon.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: sun and moon letter cards in two colours. Stretch: explain why the shaddah appears after a silent laam.

lessons.unit: Unit 3: Laam and stopping signs
lessons.title: Stopping signs in the mushaf
objectives: Recognise six stopping signs
Choose where to stop and continue
Start again correctly after stopping

keywords.def: a sign meaning you should stop: م

starter: How do you stop on a word ending with tanween fathah?

teach.heading: Why signs matter
bullets: Stopping in the wrong place may change the meaning
They were added to help readers
teach.note: Remind pupils that stopping at the wrong place can create a wrong meaning, so we respect the signs. Example type: stopping at 'there is no god' before 'except Allah' would be a serious meaning mistake. Use that as a teaching hook without reciting it.

teach.heading: The six signs
teach.note: Draw each sign on the board. Pupils find them in the mushaf. Ask: which is the strongest stop? The m sign.

teach.heading: More signs
bullets: ∴ - stop at one of the two places
teach.note: Explain three more. The three dots form a pair: you may stop at one of them but not both. Show an example in the mushaf. Pupils copy the signs.

teach.heading: How to stop
bullets: Stop on the last letter of the word
teach.note: Model stopping on a word. Example: stopping on الرَّحِيمِ gives 'rahim' with a sukoon. Round ة: stopping on رَحْمَة gives 'rahmah'. Practise.

practice: What does the sign م mean?
Which sign tells you not to stop?
independent: Mark the signs on a printed page of Al-Ma'un or Al-Humazah
Recite and stop at each sign
Quiz: sign cards matched to meanings
exit: How do we stop on ة?
lessons.homework: Find and name three stopping signs in the mushaf page you are reading.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: sign flash cards with colours. Stretch: explain why the three dots must be treated as a pair.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Recitation of Al-Kafirun and An-Nasr
lessons.title: Surat Al-Kafirun
objectives: Recite Al-Kafirun accurately
Apply the makharij and madd learned
Understand its message
starter: Name a sun letter and a moon letter.

teach.heading: The surah
teach.note: Introduce the theme: clear belief and respect. The Prophet ﷺ was told to say these words. Chunk and echo the first two ayat. Mention madd munfasil in يَا أَيُّهَا.

teach.heading: Ayat 3-5
teach.note: Notice the repetition: ayah 3 and ayah 5 are the same. This is helpful for memorising. Explain that the repetition stresses the difference between worshipping Allah alone and worshipping others.

teach.heading: Ayah 6
bullets: Your way is yours, mine is mine
teach.note: The final ayah draws a clear line. Remind pupils that Islam teaches us to be clear about worship of Allah alone while behaving with respect and justice to everyone. Ask: how can we do both?

teach.heading: Rules to find
teach.note: Pupils label أَنتُمْ (noon sakinah before ta = ikhfa). Madd letters appear in عَابِدُونَ. In لَكُمْ دِينُكُمْ the meem sakinah meets daal: izhar shafawi, so say the meem clearly. Practise slowly with echo.

practice: What do ayat 3 and 5 have in common?
independent: Read Al-Kafirun with a partner; mark ikhfa and madd
Memorise ayat 1-3 with listen/read/cover
Individual recitation
lessons.homework: Recite Al-Kafirun daily and learn ayat 1-5 by heart.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio and a repetition map. Stretch: learn the whole surah and explain ayah 6.

lessons.unit: Unit 4: Recitation of Al-Kafirun and An-Nasr
lessons.title: Surat An-Nasr
objectives: Recite An-Nasr accurately
Apply tajweed rules from the term
Reflect on gratitude after success
starter: Name the four ways to join isti'adha and basmalah.

teach.heading: The surah
bullets: وَرَأَيْتَ النَّاسَ يَدْخُلُونَ فِي دِينِ اللَّهِ أَفْوَاجًا
teach.note: Meaning: when the help of Allah and the victory come, and you see people entering the religion of Allah in crowds. Chunk and echo.

teach.heading: Ayah 3
teach.note: Meaning: glorify your Lord with praise and ask forgiveness; He is ever accepting of repentance. When blessings come, the response is humility, praise and istighfar.

teach.heading: Rules to find
teach.note: Pupils find the rules. The ghayn in وَاسْتَغْفِرْهُ is a heavy letter. In جَاءَ the madd muttasil is four counts. Ask which heavy letters appear.

teach.heading: Lesson from the surah
teach.note: Discuss how to respond to success, for example when we do well in a test. Link to humility. Keep the discussion short and sincere.

independent: Read An-Nasr aloud and mark the heavy letters
Memorise ayat 1-2, then ayah 3
Recite An-Nasr and Al-Kafirun together
exit: What do we do when blessings come?
Name a heavy letter in An-Nasr.
lessons.homework: Recite An-Nasr daily, then say 'alhamdulillah' for one success each day.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: chunked audio and sentence stems for gratitude. Stretch: write two sentences on how the surah teaches humility.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Al-Balad and idgham
lessons.title: Surat Al-Layl 92:1-7: hear, understand and memorise
lessons.bigQuestion: Night and day are opposites. Can you think of other opposites Allah made? Why might He swear by them?
objectives: To memorise Al-Layl 92:1-7 accurately and recite it with its tajweed
successCriteria: All: recite 92:1-7 after the teacher, word for word
Most: recite 92:1-7 from memory with no more than one prompt
Some: link 92:1-7 to the ayat before and name the tajweed rules in them
lessons.smsc: Moral: giving generously and the promise that Allah makes the way easy for the giver

hook.text: Night and day are opposites. Can you think of other opposites Allah made? Why might He swear by them?
hook.a: Night and day, male and female, giving and holding back: Allah swears by them to make us think (92:1 to 4).

islamicLink.text: Allah swears by the night, the day and His creation, then says: 'Indeed, your efforts are diverse' (Al-Layl 92:4). The one who gives, fears Allah and believes in the best reward, Allah will ease his way (92:5 to 7).

starter.q: How many ayat are in Surat Al-Qadr (سورة القدر)?

teach.heading: New ayat: Al-Layl 92:1-7
bullets: Listen first: the teacher recites twice
Follow each word with your finger
teach.note: Begin with isti'adhah and Bismillah. Recite 92:1-7 slowly twice from the mushaf (spoken recitation only, no melody exercises), pointing to each word on the shared screen. The Arabic is the Qur'an in Uthmani script (Hafs 'an 'Asim, Madinah mushaf); check it against the school mushaf.

quote.text: وَٱلَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ (١) وَٱلنَّهَارِ إِذَا تَجَلَّىٰ (٢) وَمَا خَلَقَ ٱلذَّكَرَ وَٱلْأُنثَىٰٓ (٣) إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّىٰ (٤) فَأَمَّا مَنْ أَعْطَىٰ وَٱتَّقَىٰ (٥) وَصَدَّقَ بِٱلْحُسْنَىٰ (٦) فَسَنُيَسِّرُهُۥ لِلْيُسْرَىٰ (٧)

teach.heading: What the ayat mean
bullets: This is a translation of the meaning, not the Qur'an itself
teach.note: Read the English slowly. Remind pupils: only the Arabic is the Qur'an; any English is a translation of its meaning (here Saheeh International).

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: By the night when it covers
And [by] the day when it appears
And [by] He who created the male and female,
As for he who gives and fears Allah
We will ease him toward ease.

teach.heading: Tajweed spotlight in today's ayat
teach.note: Point to each word in the mushaf. Pupils say the rule before you do.

head: Word
Where
Rule
How to read it
rows: Clear noon, then a heavy ط
Full mouth; the د stays light

teach.heading: Listen and repeat: mics in turn
teach.note: Talaqqi (تلقي): learning recitation by hearing it from the teacher. Work through 92:1-7 one ayah at a time. Keep a visible order of names (the register) so every pupil gets a turn across the week. Unmute only the pupils whose turn it is; everyone else whispers along with mics muted.
cycle: Teacher recites one ayah (talaqqi)
Pupils listen, mics muted, eyes on the words
Mics on in turn: three pupils repeat in register order
Teacher corrects one point for each
Whole class repeats softly, then moves to the next ayah

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.q: 92:5 to 7 say Allah will ease the way of the one who ...
check.why: 92:5 to 7: the one who gives, fears Allah and believes in the best reward. Keeping money back is the opposite, in 92:8.

practice.q: Chunk and link Al-Layl 92:1-7 together, ayah by ayah.
practice.a: The class recites 92:1-7 together without the mushaf.
practice.model: I do: chunk 92:1-7. Ayah 1: 3 times looking, 3 times without looking. Then ayah 2 the same way. Then link: recite 1 and 2 together twice. Finish by reciting the whole chunk once without the mushaf.

practice.q: «يَغْشَىٰ» starts with a heavy letter. Which?
practice.a: غ

independent.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 92:1-7 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
independent.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.
independent.model: The teacher shows the 3-3-link method once: read the ayah 3 times looking, say it 3 times without looking, then link it to the ayah before it. Rota: names on screen, about 90 seconds each, so every pupil is heard at least once a week; the teacher marks the rubric and gives one target.

independent.q: On the pupil PDF, circle every heavy letter in 92:1 to 7.
Explain in one sentence what 'your efforts are diverse' (92:4) means.
independent.a: People work towards different things: some for good, some for bad.

exit.q: Al-Layl 92:5: «فَأَمَّا مَنْ ...» Which word comes next?
exit.a: أَعْطَىٰ

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Night and day are opposites. Can you think of other opposites Allah made? Why might He swear by them?
exit.a: Night and day, male and female, giving and holding back: Allah swears by them to make us think (92:1 to 4).

lessons.homework: Recite Al-Layl 92:1-7 to a parent three times a day and revise Surahs 114 to 93 and Ayat al-Kursi (today's rota group); tick the portal revision log each day.
lessons.send: SEND: shorter chunks (one ayah), the pupil PDF with each word spaced, extra listening turn. EAL: key words with meanings beside the Arabic. Stretch: link to the next ayat and explain one rule to the class.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Al-Balad and idgham
lessons.title: Heavy letters: reciting with a full mouth
lessons.bigQuestion: Say 'saad' and then 'seen'. One sounds full and deep, one sounds thin. Which is which, and what did your tongue do?
objectives: To understand which letters are always heavy and how to say them with a full mouth
successCriteria: All: name the seven heavy letters
Most: say each heavy letter with a full, raised tongue
Some: find heavy letters in Al-Layl 92:1 to 7
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: honouring Allah's words by giving every letter its right

keywords.def: the tongue rising: what makes a letter heavy

hook.text: Say 'saad' and then 'seen'. One sounds full and deep, one sounds thin. Which is which, and what did your tongue do?
hook.a: Saad (ص) is heavy: the back of the tongue rises and the mouth fills. Seen (س) is light.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Indeed, We have sent it down as an Arabic Qur'an so that you might understand' (Yusuf 12:2). Each Arabic letter has its own sound; changing a heavy letter to a light one can change the word.

starter.q: Recite Al-Layl 92:4 in your head. How does the next ayah begin?

teach.heading: Seven heavy letters
bullets: خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ
Remember them as خُصَّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ
teach.note: Bismillah. Tafkheem (تفخيم) means making a letter heavy. The back of the tongue rises towards the roof of the mouth, so the sound fills the mouth.

teach.heading: How to make it heavy
teach.note: Ask pupils to put a hand under the chin: on heavy letters the tongue lifts. Never round the lips into an 'o'.
cycle: Lift the back of the tongue
Fill the mouth with the sound
Keep the lips natural, not round
Say the vowel full: qaa, not kaa

teach.heading: Heavy letters in Al-Layl
teach.note: Read each word; pupils echo with mics in turn.

teach.heading: Common mistake
teach.note: Show the difference with the lips: heavy is from the tongue, not from rounding.

misconception.wrong: Rounding the lips to sound heavy: 'qoo-la'
misconception.right: Lift the back of the tongue; lips stay natural: 'qaa-la'

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Read the results, then explain the right answer.

check.q: Which of these is a heavy letter?
check.why: ط is one of خُصَّ ضَغْطٍ قِظْ. ت and ك are light: they are its light partners.

practice.q: Say «وَصَدَّقَ» (92:6) and name the heavy letters.
practice.a: ص and ق are heavy; و and د are light.
practice.model: I do: و light. صَ: lift the back of the tongue, full mouth. دّ: light. قَ: heavy, full mouth. So two heavy letters: ص and ق.

practice.q: How many heavy letters are always heavy?

independent.q: Heavy letter hunt (pupil PDF): circle the heavy letters in Al-'Alaq 96:1 to 5. Today's rota group recites 92:1 to 7 to the teacher in turn.
independent.model: The teacher circles the first: ٱقْرَأْ in 96:1 has qaf, a heavy letter.

independent.q: Extend: write the seven heavy letters from memory.
independent.a: خ ص ض غ ط ق ظ

independent.q: Stretch: which heavy letter is in «ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ»? Trick question: explain.
independent.a: None: ع and ل are light here (the laam is only heavy in the Name Allah after fathah or dammah).

exit.q: Which word has a heavy letter?
exit.a: خَلَقَ

exit.q: Back to our ponder: Say 'saad' and then 'seen'. One sounds full and deep, one sounds thin. Which is which, and what did your tongue do?
exit.a: Saad (ص) is heavy: the back of the tongue rises and the mouth fills. Seen (س) is light.

lessons.homework: Say the seven heavy letters to a parent with a full mouth, then recite Al-Layl 92:1 to 7; tick the revision log.
lessons.send: SEND: rule card with letters in colour, the pupil PDF with examples spaced out, extra listening turn. EAL: key words with meanings beside the Arabic. Stretch: find and explain an example in a surah not on the slides.

lessons.title: Surat Al-Layl 92:8-14: hear, understand and memorise
lessons.bigQuestion: Someone has plenty but will not share. Does his money help him in the end?
objectives: To memorise Al-Layl 92:8-14 accurately and recite it with its tajweed
successCriteria: All: recite 92:8-14 after the teacher, word for word

hook.text: When Allah gives a person a lot, he says 'my Lord honoured me'; when less, 'my Lord humiliated me' (89:15 to 16). Is wealth really how Allah shows honour?
hook.a: No: both ease and hardship are tests. Honour is in faith and good deeds, such as honouring the orphan and feeding the poor (89:17 to 18).

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'No! But you do not honor the orphan' 'And you do not encourage one another to feed the poor.' (Al-Fajr 89:17 to 18).

teach.note: Read the English slowly. Remind pupils: only the Arabic is the Qur'an; any English is a translation of its meaning (here Saheeh International).

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: So your Lord poured upon them a scourge of punishment.
Indeed, your Lord is in observation.
And as for man, when his Lord tries him and [thus] is generous to him and favors him, he says, "My Lord has honored me."
But when He tries him and restricts his provision, he says, "My Lord has humiliated me."
No! But you do not honor the orphan
And you do not encourage one another to feed the poor.

teach.heading: Tajweed spotlight in today's ayat
teach.note: Point to each word in the mushaf. Pupils say the rule before you do.

teach.heading: Listen and repeat: mics in turn
teach.note: Talaqqi (تلقي): learning recitation by hearing it from the teacher. Work through 89:13-18 one ayah at a time. Keep a visible order of names (the register) so every pupil gets a turn across the week. Unmute only the pupils whose turn it is; everyone else whispers along with mics muted.
cycle: Teacher recites one ayah (talaqqi)
Pupils listen, mics muted, eyes on the words
Mics on in turn: three pupils repeat in register order
Teacher corrects one point for each
Whole class repeats softly, then moves to the next ayah

teach.heading: Quick check

check.q: 89:17 to 18 blame people for not ...
options: honouring the orphan and feeding the poor
check.why: 89:17 to 18: you do not honour the orphan, and you do not encourage one another to feed the poor.

practice.q: Chunk and link Al-Fajr 89:13-18 together, ayah by ayah.
practice.a: The class recites 89:13-18 together without the mushaf.
practice.model: I do: chunk 89:13-18. Ayah 13: 3 times looking, 3 times without looking. Then ayah 14 the same way. Then link: recite 13 and 14 together twice. Finish by reciting the whole chunk once without the mushaf.

practice.q: «تَحَٰٓضُّونَ» (89:18) has a long madd because ...
practice.a: a shaddah follows the alif
options: a hamza is in the next word

independent.q: Listening rota: today's group recites 89:13-18 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: 3-3-link the same ayat, then tick the revision log.
independent.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.
independent.model: The teacher shows the 3-3-link method once: read the ayah 3 times looking, say it 3 times without looking, then link it to the ayah before it. Rota: names on screen, about 90 seconds each, so every pupil is heard at least once a week; the teacher marks the rubric and gives one target.

independent.q: Recite Al-Fajr 89:1 to 18 to a partner. Partner ticks each ayah.
independent.a: Eighteen ticks; slips noted for home revision.

independent.q: Name all the madds in 89:15 to 16.
independent.a: Munfasil: رَبِّىٓ أَكْرَمَنِ, وَأَمَّآ إِذَا, رَبِّىٓ أَهَٰنَنِ; natural: مَا, ٱبْتَلَىٰهُ, فَيَقُولُ and others.

exit.q: Al-Fajr 89:17: «كَلَّا بَل ...» Which word comes next?
exit.a: لَّا

exit.q: Back to our ponder: When Allah gives a person a lot, he says 'my Lord honoured me'; when less, 'my Lord humiliated me' (89:15 to 16). Is wealth really how Allah shows honour?
exit.a: No: both ease and hardship are tests. Honour is in faith and good deeds, such as honouring the orphan and feeding the poor (89:17 to 18).

check.why: Yaa at the end of رَبِّىٓ, hamza at the start of the next word: munfasil.

practice.q: Recite Al-Fajr 89:13 to 18 together, holding the madd lazim in 89:18 for 6 counts.
practice.a: The class recites 89:13 to 18 with the long madd in تَحَٰٓضُّونَ.
practice.model: I do: تَحَٰٓضُّونَ: the alif is followed by a shaddah, so I stretch six counts: ta-haaaaaaa-dduna.
